You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 1 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v006

Define both predicates precisely, including entity unit, eligible subtypes, exclusions and effective dates. Start sequentially with one X search, one Y search and one conjunction search. Maintain deduplicated dual frontiers and a ledger of canonical identities, aliases, evidence for each predicate, unresolved facts and estimated next-action cost. Group pending candidates into meaningful cohorts by their discovery source or eligibility subtype; do not invent arbitrary cohorts when none are useful. Separate evidence-backed near-intersections from speculative candidates that satisfy only one predicate. Resolve near-intersections first. For a speculative cohort, check at most three diverse candidates before committing more spend, and limit each dispatch to 10% of the initial budget; a single necessary check may exceed that cap if affordable. Inspect returned evidence before dispatching another sample. If a sample yields no verified addition or materially improved evidence, park that cohort and test another partition or the reverse frontier. No-hit candidates remain unresolved, not rejected. Revisit a parked cohort when new evidence, an alias or a demonstrably different source gives a better resolution path; a failed sample never proves the cohort empty. Expand productive cohorts in similarly small rounds, comparing verified additions and evidence progress per actual spend against discovery alternatives. Retain one neglected-cohort or reverse-frontier probe after two productive rounds so early samples do not permanently starve rare subtypes. After two discovery queries add no plausible identities, change source, subtype or frontier rather than paraphrasing the conjunction. Reuse established facts and never repeat settled checks. Keep at least 35% of initial budget for verification and evidence resolution, and stop discovery earlier if the promising pending queue requires it. End with identity, scope and date checks; submit only individually supported intersections and do not infer completeness from sampling or search saturation.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].
Use Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact-name checks and first-pass check_candidates. Request identity-matched evidence for both tests while directing retrieval to the missing fact. Estimate dispatch cost per candidate and provider, not per tool invocation; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Escalate only individual promising unresolved cases to Exa alone with 4 results after a cheap check or targeted fetch fails; never escalate a whole cohort because one member is ambiguous. Following baseline sampling and genuine Parallel stagnation, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if the resolution reserve remains intact; retain Exa discovery only for useful incremental evidence or identities. No broad auto-routing or routine concurrent variants. Domain filters belong on targeted evidence checks, with relaxation when necessary, not the entire discovery frontier. Use publication-date filters only when publication date defines eligibility; check effective dates in source content.

### Fetch policy
Cache facts and URLs. Fetch when source content can resolve a material identity or predicate uncertainty, or a discovered list supplies several plausible candidates. Prefer authoritative pages and shared evidence that reduces pending-check cost, without turning source bundles into the mandatory discovery unit. Do not fetch every result. After a blocked or uninformative page, try one targeted alternate source rather than a fetch chain.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

  - Python execution: `uv run python ...`
  - Scripts and tests: `uv run ...`

  - Python CLI tools: `uvx <tool>`

  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

</addendum>

sections.preamble:
You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 1 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v006

Define both predicates precisely, including entity unit, eligible subtypes, exclusions and effective dates. Start sequentially with one X search, one Y search and one conjunction search. Maintain deduplicated dual frontiers and a ledger of canonical identities, aliases, evidence for each predicate, unresolved facts and estimated next-action cost. Group pending candidates into meaningful cohorts by their discovery source or eligibility subtype; do not invent arbitrary cohorts when none are useful. Separate evidence-backed near-intersections from speculative candidates that satisfy only one predicate. Resolve near-intersections first. For a speculative cohort, check at most three diverse candidates before committing more spend, and limit each dispatch to 10% of the initial budget; a single necessary check may exceed that cap if affordable. Inspect returned evidence before dispatching another sample. If a sample yields no verified addition or materially improved evidence, park that cohort and test another partition or the reverse frontier. No-hit candidates remain unresolved, not rejected. Revisit a parked cohort when new evidence, an alias or a demonstrably different source gives a better resolution path; a failed sample never proves the cohort empty. Expand productive cohorts in similarly small rounds, comparing verified additions and evidence progress per actual spend against discovery alternatives. Retain one neglected-cohort or reverse-frontier probe after two productive rounds so early samples do not permanently starve rare subtypes. After two discovery queries add no plausible identities, change source, subtype or frontier rather than paraphrasing the conjunction. Reuse established facts and never repeat settled checks. Keep at least 35% of initial budget for verification and evidence resolution, and stop discovery earlier if the promising pending queue requires it. End with identity, scope and date checks; submit only individually supported intersections and do not infer completeness from sampling or search saturation.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].
Use Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact-name checks and first-pass check_candidates. Request identity-matched evidence for both tests while directing retrieval to the missing fact. Estimate dispatch cost per candidate and provider, not per tool invocation; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Escalate only individual promising unresolved cases to Exa alone with 4 results after a cheap check or targeted fetch fails; never escalate a whole cohort because one member is ambiguous. Cache facts and URLs. Fetch when source content can resolve a material identity or predicate uncertainty, or a discovered list supplies several plausible candidates. Prefer authoritative pages and shared evidence that reduces pending-check cost, without turning source bundles into the mandatory discovery unit. Do not fetch every result. After a blocked or uninformative page, try one targeted alternate source rather than a fetch chain.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

lessons.title: Source-derived vocabulary offers a bounded repair for uninformative samples
lessons.body: Hypothesis, not a measured improvement: distinguish an unproductive cohort from a query that fails to express the source's terminology. Stanford's relevance-feedback guidance identifies synonymy as a recall problem (https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/html/htmledition/relevance-feedback-and-query-expansion-1.html); systematic-search guidance recommends harvesting terminology and testing retrieval against known relevant records (https://library.cumc.columbia.edu/kb/developing-and-validating-comprehensive-literature). Adapt this with one bounded repair using terms actually observed in relevant evidence, not unlimited paraphrases. Retrieval of known positives diagnoses a route but cannot establish completeness or validate other candidates. No unseen-hunt benefit has yet been demonstrated.

candidates.rationale: Evidence-conditioned query repair: retain v006's interruptible sampling but make a zero-progress sample trigger a bounded vocabulary diagnostic when relevant source evidence supports one. This changes how samples are interpreted, rather than requiring a census, source bundles, or a terminal residual-coverage pass. Harvest source-native relationship labels, identifiers and aliases to improve later missing-fact checks and reopen selected parked candidates. Parallel's attributed 135 correct/dollar versus Exa's 56.8 supports keeping cheap retrieval as the default, not a causal quality claim. The improvement remains untested.
candidates.instructions:
Define X and Y precisely, including entity unit, eligible subtypes, exclusions and effective dates. Start sequentially with one X search, one Y search and one conjunction search. Maintain deduplicated dual frontiers and a ledger of canonical identities, aliases, predicate evidence, unresolved facts, retrieval formulations and estimated next-action cost. Anchor spending on evidence-backed near-intersections before speculative one-sided candidates. Group candidates only into meaningful discovery-source or subtype cohorts.
Add an evidence-derived vocabulary map for each predicate: record source-native relationship terms, registry identifiers, historical names and aliases actually encountered in relevant material. Keep these separate from eligibility rules: retrieval vocabulary may change, eligibility must not. Prefer a candidate's name or stable identifier plus the missing relationship, not a query requiring both predicates to appear on one page. Use known evidence without paying to reverify settled facts.
For a speculative cohort, sample at most three diverse candidates, with each dispatch capped at 10% of initial budget except a necessary affordable single check. Inspect evidence before continuing. On zero verified additions or material evidence progress, distinguish explicit disqualifying evidence from absent or off-topic retrieval. For absent/off-topic retrieval, allow one cheap repair only if cached relevant evidence supplies a concrete alternative term, identifier or alias. Retry the most promising unresolved sampled candidate with that evidence-derived formulation. This repair must replace, not supplement, the next exploratory action and remains within the dispatch cap. If no supported alternative exists or the repair adds no evidence, park the cohort and change frontier or partition. Do not generate synonym lists or repeated conjunction paraphrases.
Where an existing known-positive record reveals why the original formulation was mismatched, diagnose this from cached evidence first. At most one paid known-positive retrieval diagnostic per hunt is allowed when its result would change several pending checks; it tests retrieval, not eligibility. A successful diagnostic is not a new find and does not justify cohort-wide retries. Reopen at most three promising parked cases when genuinely new source vocabulary creates a distinct resolution path; continue only after useful incremental evidence.
Expand productive cohorts in small rounds, comparing verified additions and evidence progress per actual spend with discovery alternatives. Retain a neglected-cohort or reverse-frontier probe after two productive rounds. After two discovery queries produce no plausible identities, change source, subtype or frontier. No-hit candidates remain unresolved, never rejected by absence alone; neither sampling nor successful diagnostics establishes completeness. Keep at least 35% of initial budget for verification and resolution, stopping discovery earlier if the pending queue requires it. End with identity, scope and effective-date checks; submit only individually evidenced intersections.
candidates.routing_rules: Use Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact-name checks, bounded query repairs and first-pass check_candidates. Pass source-derived terminology only where supported and direct checks to missing facts while retaining identity-matched evidence for both predicates. Estimate spend per candidate and provider; lower result counts do not imply lower cost. A vocabulary repair is optional and must not become a mandatory extra step before escalation. Escalate individual promising unresolved candidates to Exa alone with 4 results after a cheap check or targeted fetch fails. Never escalate an entire cohort. After baseline sampling and genuine Parallel stagnation, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if the resolution reserve remains intact; continue only for incremental evidence or identities. No routine concurrent variants or broad auto-routing. Apply domain filters to targeted evidence retrieval, relaxing them when necessary, not to the entire discovery frontier. Publication-date filters apply only when publication date defines eligibility; otherwise inspect effective dates in source content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Cache URLs, facts and source-native terminology. Fetch when content can resolve material identity or predicate uncertainty, expose relevant relationship labels, or provide several plausible candidates. Prefer authoritative sources and shared evidence that reduces pending-check cost, without making source bundles mandatory. Do not fetch solely to build an exhaustive vocabulary map or fetch every result. After a blocked or uninformative page, try one targeted alternate source rather than a fetch chain. Historical terminology can aid retrieval but cannot substitute for evidence of current eligibility.
